concept: A rout explained by how the goals were scored, not just how many. The hero puts the scoreline in muted grey (Seven goals against Thailand.) and the reason in white (Six came from set pieces.), so the why lands before any detail. Slide 2 splits the seven goals into three bars: four penalty corners, two penalty strokes and a single goal from open play, so the gap between set pieces and open play is the picture. Slide 3 gives Deepika's hat-trick one giant 3, slide 4 shows the table where India and Japan are level on 9 points and India lead on goal difference, and the last slide moves to China on Tuesday. caption:
Seven goals against Thailand. Six came from set pieces.

Defending champions India beat Thailand 7-0 in Bhopal on Sunday to reach the semi-finals of the Women's Asian Champions Trophy with two group games to spare.

Why it was so one-sided: India kept winning set pieces and kept scoring from them. Deepika scored a hat-trick of penalty corner goals (10th, 11th and 56th minutes). Navneet Kaur converted two penalty strokes (4th and 56th). Sunelita Toppo added a penalty corner in the 32nd. Mumtaz Khan's 28th-minute strike was the only goal from open play.

It was 3-0 after 11 minutes and 4-0 at half-time.

India have 9 points from 3 wins (4-1 Malaysia, 2-1 South Korea, 7-0 Thailand) and top the table on goal difference, +11 to Japan's +6. Both are through. India play China on Tuesday, November 24.
